items.briefing:
Scammers are getting more creative — a current warning highlights that attackers are now sending phishing attacks through calendar invites using .ics files. If you receive an unexpected meeting invitation, especially from an unknown sender, be cautious about clicking any links inside it. This method is designed to bypass standard email security filters, making it harder for your organisation's defences to catch automatically.

Australian staff should also stay alert to ScamWatch advisories, which continue to track emerging threats targeting Australians. **Practical tip:** Before accepting any calendar invite, verify the sender directly — if it looks unexpected or unusual, delete it without clicking any links.

featured.title: Barracuda warns calendar invites are being used for phishing via .ics files
featured.quote: Calendar invites used for phishing represents new attack vector affecting all Australian organisations.
